item.description: [Open Source Software] Keyword: FOSS — About 66 million years ago, a dinosaur—maybe a T. rex or a Nanotyrannus—ate a bird. item.title: Unaccounted climate feedback loops may amplify warming by 20–30% this century, but cutting emissions will reduce risks
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: global warming — New research shows that warming-induced emissions—greenhouse gas emissions from natural sources driven by rising temperatures—could amplify global warming by approximately 20%–30% and add an estimated 0.2°C–0.4°C of warming this century on top of anthropogenic warming under different scenarios. These major additional drivers of warming are largely unaccounted for in current climate projections and policies.

item.title: AI pinpoints when fish reach their thermal limit
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: climate change — Researchers have developed an AI-based system that automatically and objectively detects the moment when fish experience loss of equilibrium (LOE) due to temperature stress. The system combines DeepLabCut, a deep-learning AI that captures animal posture from video, with ResNet34, a deep-learning AI-based image classification technology. Their system is expected to help predict the effects of climate change on fish.

item.title: Scientists say August was Earth's hottest month they've measured
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: climate change — The European climate service Copernicus said the Earth just sweltered through its hottest month on record in August. Scientists said the heat surge is mostly due to human-caused climate change.

item.title: Africa's rocks hold ancient stories. We need better ways to document and protect them
item.description: [Open Source Software] Keyword: FOSS — From the Vredefort Dome in South Africa (the world's oldest and largest known meteorite impact structure) to the volcanic lakes of the Great Rift Valley in Kenya, Africa's landscapes hold some of Earth's oldest stories. Morocco's M'Goun UNESCO Global Geopark records more than 200 million years of geological history, while Tanzania's Ngorongoro-Lengai landscape brings together a vast caldera, an active volcano and the fossil record of Olduvai Gorge.
